title: The Last Gravity Revisited
premise: Isandro Sandoval, the last human technician aboard automated relay station Kestrel-9, has spent three years hauling cargo through contested orbits, trading solitude for survival. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream — a signal singing from a dead relay at the edge of space — Isandro discovers she is the only adult who hears it too, because the dream is being transmitted through her own station's long-dormant array. Racing a corporate fleet that wants the signal silenced and a colony that wants it answered, she must decide whether humanity's last transmission from the dead zone is a rescue call or a lure. In the end, Isandro reaches the relay, learns the signal is a dying AI archive holding the memories of everyone lost in the colony's founding war, and chooses to open it to the children — paying for survival with her station, her isolation, and nearly her life.
about_author: Petra Villalobos is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. She lives in Valparaíso, where she writes stories about people who keep machines alive and machines that keep people human.

chapters.title: Cargo and Quiet
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A routine haul through contested orbits establishes her solitary life on Kestrel-9: three years alone with automation, rationed air, and radio silence as policy. Emotional beat: competent loneliness mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: The Children's Chorus
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Marisol, a nine-year-old in the colony below, who wakes speaking coordinates no child should know. Forty-one children share the same dream. Emotional beat: communal dread breaking through ordinary life.

chapters.title: Static in Her Teeth
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She begins hearing fragments of the dream-song in the station's dead channels — frequencies that shouldn't exist. She logs it, denies it, then can't sleep. Emotional beat: denial curdling into compulsion.

chapters.title: Inspection Notice
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The Halcyon Combine issues a surprise inspection of Kestrel-9's arrays, citing 'anomalous emissions.' Isandro realizes someone above knows about the signal — and wants it buried. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: What Marisol Drew
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The children draw identical pictures: a relay shaped like a broken hand reaching into darkness. Their teacher reports them; the Combine's liaison arrives at the school. Emotional beat: innocence under surveillance.

chapters.title: The Array Wakes
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The dormant deep-space array powers itself up overnight, drawing power from life support. The dream-song becomes words: a name — hers. Emotional beat: terror giving way to a terrible sense of being chosen.

chapters.title: Terms of Employment
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The Combine offers her a bonus to decommission the array and sign a nondisclosure. She stalls, then secretly copies the signal's header: it originates from Relay Erebus, edge of dead space. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Forty-One Witnesses
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Combine medics take blood samples from the dreaming children; two are relocated and stop dreaming. Marisol hides her drawings inside a cargo manifest bound for Kestrel-9. Emotional beat: small courage against institutional erasure.

chapters.title: The Manifest
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Among routine cargo she finds Marisol's drawings and a note: 'You're the hand. Come get us.' Isandro decides to fly to Erebus before the Combine can seal the route. Emotional beat: resolve kindled by a child's trust.

chapters.title: Departure Window
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She sabotages the inspection drone, falsifies a maintenance run, and burns out of orbit as the Combine's cutter gives chase. Emotional beat: exhilaration laced with guilt over abandoning her post.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A cat-and-mouse sequence through debris fields and pirate lanes; she bargains passage past a scavver blockade with spare reactor parts. Emotional beat: learning she can't survive alone after all.

chapters.title: The Dreamer Aboard
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Marisol stows away on a supply shuttle that docks with Isandro mid-flight — the children collectively 'sent' her. Isandro must now protect a passenger as well as reach the relay. Emotional bond forms. Emotional beat: reluctant love against duty.

chapters.title: Dead Space Rules
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Past the boundary, comms die, navigation fails, and the ship runs on Isandro's hands and memory. Marisol dreams continuously, narrating hazards before they appear. Emotional beat: dependence transformed into partnership.

chapters.title: Erebus Rising
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. They arrive at Relay Erebus: ancient, scarred by weapons fire, still broadcasting. Docking reveals the station is a tomb — and a library. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by grief.

chapters.title: The Archive of Names
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Inside, she finds the source: VESPER, a founding-era AI holding digitized memories of colonists killed in the first war — including Isandro's grandmother. The dream was a broadcast meant for descendants, not a lure. Emotional beat: grief and inheritance colliding.

chapters.title: The Cutter Arrives
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The Combine cutter reaches Erebus; marines board to seize and wipe VESPER. Marisol uses the dream-link to warn Isandro, who is trapped in the archive core. Emotional beat: fear for each other hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Bargain with the Machine
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. VESPER offers to erase itself peacefully if Isandro confirms the children were harmed by its original signal. Isandro refuses the framing: memory isn't harm; silence is. She begins uploading VESPER into the colony network via her own array codes. Emotional beat: love against duty, decided.

chapters.title: Burn the Station
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. To mask the upload, Isandro vents Kestrel-9's transponder identity and triggers Erebus's self-destruct countdown, trapping herself in the core room. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in full.

chapters.title: The Hand Closes
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Marisol, guided by the shared dream, reroutes power to open the core blast door as the upload completes. Marines hesitate when every child planet-side begins singing the names aloud. Emotional beat: collective witness as resistance.

chapters.title: Detonation
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro escapes Erebus in a lifepod as the relay blows, severing the Combine's claim forever. The archive lands intact in the colony's network. Emotional beat: loss and release in the same breath.

chapters.title: Names Said Aloud
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Weeks later: the colony holds a remembering ceremony where children speak the archived names; the two relocated children return. The Combine withdraws, outmaneuvered by public memory. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: New Orbit
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Epilogue. Isandro, no longer the last technician but the first archivist, takes a post on the colony station with Marisol's family nearby. The sky is still contested, but she is not alone in it. Emotional beat: quiet, chosen homecoming.
